claims.assertion: The trip is a RydeTAXI metered ride (metered fare structure billed as base + distance + time in F7), so detour distance enters the fare directly, as stated in RD-0/RD-2; the rider was charged $40.45.

GPS shows one off-route segment 08:42–08:54 adding 4.74 km (7.24 km driven where the optimal route is 2.50 km, deviating up to 1568 m), on a trip that ran 19.0 km against an optimal 13.9 km (+5.1 km, +37%).

The rider's agreement (F9 '可以，走 Balestier Road 吧。' at 08:40) is expressly limited to Balestier Road only, but no record — no stop, no located message, no road-name fact — places the 08:42–08:54 segment on Balestier Road, so under G13/RD-5 the tie between the agreed road and the driven segment is undetermined and the exemption is not made out; the segment is therefore an unexempted detour.

The only justification offered is the driver's post-trip statement that he informed the rider (F8, F11); under RD-4 a reroute claim needs a traffic incident on the replaced optimal route, and F15 records no traffic incidents near the route during the trip window.

The expressway congestion relied on is at most a speed-band record (F12, Central Expressway band 2 during 08:21–08:42), which the policy accepts only as corroboration and not as a standalone exemption, and the record itself ends at 08:42 when the deviation begins.

Because the unexempted segment added 4.74 km and the trip's per-km rate is $1.4098 (F4: $7.22 ÷ 5.12 km), the rider is owed that mileage: 4.74 × $1.4098 ≈ $6.68 SGD, to be refunded as a voucher; the billed excess-distance figure ($7.22 for 5.12 km, F4) shows how the detour was charged.
Profile facts (rider F17, driver F18, with 0 prior upheld disputes on either side) are offered only as context and are not relied on for the finding or for any flag_account request.

claims.assertion: The only off-route segment in this trip is F3 (08:42–08:54, +4.74 km), and the rider's own message F9 ('可以，走 Balestier Road 吧') was sent at 08:40 — before that segment started at 08:42 — in reply to the driver's ask in F8 naming Balestier Road, so the segment is covered by a pre-segment route agreement.

The reason for the reroute was real congestion on the optimal corridor, not an errand: Central Expressway was at speed band 2 (10–19 km/h) during 08:21–08:42 per F12, exactly the jam the driver cited in F8, and the alternatives he stayed on (Ang Mo Kio Ave 8 and Ave 1) ran at band 5 (40–49 km/h) per F13 and F14.

The detour was not a driver errand or a stop: the record shows a single through-driving loop on Balestier Road and no stop, detour to a shop or off-route halt by the driver, and weather was fair (F16) so no other cause was needed.

The rider's complaint that the fare was 'much more than the estimate' is a metered-fare consequence, not overcharging by the driver: the charged $40.45 in F7 is the sum of the published components (base $3.90, distance $26.80, time $8.17, waiting $0.11, platform $1.47) with no surge (F6, 1.0×) and no unpublished item added, so FARE-1 is not engaged.

Even at most the excess distance component is $7.22 (F4: 5.12 km × $1.4098/km), so the rider's loss is at most the mileage part of an agreed reroute — and if the segment is exempt under RD-5 the amount refundable is zero and the correct outcome is no_action.
